query_snapshot: For hydrogen chloride, which barriers does the archived NIOSH table place in its 8-hour and 4-hour groups, and what additional hazard language appears in the entry?
final_answer:
Evidence-grounded answer:

- Archived NIOSH CPC table lists these 8-hour barrier materials for hydrogen chloride: Butyl; Teflon; Saranex; Barricade; Responder; Trellchem; Tychem. [NIOSH Recommendations for Chemical Protective Clothing A-Z | NIOSH | CDC: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/ncpc/azncpc.html]
- Archived NIOSH CPC table lists these 4-hour barrier materials for hydrogen chloride: Neoprene; PVC. [NIOSH Recommendations for Chemical Protective Clothing A-Z | NIOSH | CDC: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/ncpc/azncpc.html]
- Additional hazard language in the hydrogen chloride entry: "Prevent skin contact (solution)/ Frostbite". [NIOSH Recommendations for Chemical Protective Clothing A-Z | NIOSH | CDC: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/ncpc/azncpc.html]
- Additional note in the entry: "Prevent possible skin freezing from direct liquid contact." [NIOSH Recommendations for Chemical Protective Clothing A-Z | NIOSH | CDC: https://archive.cdc.gov/www_cdc_gov/niosh/ncpc/azncpc.html]
